<section class="section" data-section="arr-growth"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Helping CFOs find</div><h2>Where is revenue accelerating?</h2><div class="q-section-layout"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">ARR growth becomes clear when you break it into its true drivers: new customers, expansion (upsell vs. cross-sell vs. pricing), and the components of churn — by cohort, by segment, by quarter.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies answer this question with anecdotes — a single large deal, a seasonal trend, a market tailwind. Revenue only truly accelerates when it’s tied to something repeatable.</p></div><div class="q-visual"><img src="https://getpacerai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/arr-waterfall-cross-sell-growth.png" alt="Where is revenue accelerating?"></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section" data-section="expansion-drivers" style="background:var(--navy-mid)"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Helping CROs understand</div><h2>What is driving our expansion ARR?</h2><div class="q-section-layout reverse"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Expansion ARR breaks into three distinct motions — upsell (more of the same), cross-sell (new products), and pricing uplift — each driven by different teams, playbooks, and signals. Knowing which motion dominates tells you whether growth is repeatable.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies report expansion as a single line. That hides whether growth comes from one whale upsell or broad-based cross-sell adoption. Mastery means decomposing expansion by motion, by product, by market — and tying each to the GTM play that produced it. Expansion only scales when you can name the motion and the muscle behind it.</p></div><div class="q-visual"><img src="https://getpacerai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/market-analysis-expansion-drivers.png" alt="What is driving our expansion ARR?"></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section" data-section="cohort-intelligence"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Cohort Intelligence</div><h2>Which cohort is our primary business driver?</h2><div class="q-section-layout"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Cohort analysis groups customers by acquisition period and tracks their revenue trajectory over time — revealing whether your business compounds from the base or erodes beneath headline growth.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies look at retention in aggregate. That masks the reality: your 2022 cohort may be expanding 115% while your 2024 cohort churns at 20%. Mastery means cutting by vintage, by segment, by market — and understanding which acquisition era built your durable base versus which is still proving itself.</p></div><div class="q-visual"><img src="https://getpacerai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/cohort-market-acct-size.png" alt="Which cohort is our primary business driver?"></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section" data-section="gross-retention" style="background:var(--navy-mid)"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Retention Drivers</div><h2>How can we improve our Gross Retention?</h2><div class="q-section-layout reverse"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Gross retention rate measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers, excluding expansion — the purest signal of whether customers stay because they need your product or leave because they don’t.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies track GRR as a single number. That tells you the symptom, not the cause. Mastery means segmenting GRR by product, by market, by account size, and by vintage — then identifying which combinations have structural churn risk versus which are operationally fixable. Retention improves when you stop treating it as one problem.</p></div><div class="q-visual"><img src="https://getpacerai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/gross-retention-vintage.png" alt="How can we improve our Gross Retention?"></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section" data-section="net-retention"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Net Retention</div><h2>How can we improve our Net Retention?</h2><div class="q-section-layout"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Net revenue retention combines expansion, contraction, and churn into a single measure of whether your existing customer base is growing or shrinking — the metric that separates compounding businesses from leaking ones.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies celebrate NRR above 100% without understanding what’s underneath. Mastery means decomposing NRR into its component motions by segment, understanding which cohorts compound and which erode, and building playbooks for each.</p></div><div class="q-visual"><img src="https://getpacerai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/net-retention-vintage.png" alt="How can we improve our Net Retention?"></div></div></div></section>

<section class="section" data-section="expansion-drivers" style="background:var(--navy-mid)"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Helping CROs understand</div><h2>What is driving our expansion ARR?</h2><div class="q-section-layout reverse"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Expansion ARR breaks into three distinct motions — upsell (more of the same), cross-sell (new products), and pricing uplift — each driven by different teams, playbooks, and signals. Knowing which motion dominates tells you whether growth is repeatable.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies report expansion as a single line. <section class="section" data-section="gross-retention" style="background:var(--navy-mid)"><div class="section-inner"><div class="section-eyebrow">Retention Drivers</div><h2>How can we improve our Gross Retention?</h2><div class="q-section-layout reverse"><div class="q-content"><p class="aeo-snippet">Gross retention rate measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers, excluding expansion — the purest signal of whether customers stay because they need your product or leave because they don’t.</p><p class="question-body">Most companies track GRR as a single number. That tells you the symptom, not the cause.
